title: Usher — 3 Pipeline
description: Ten panels, mixed by design: Prometheus for rates and depths, Postgres for the queue's and the reconciler's own breakdowns. Two of these panels read a series whose label is not the one a reader of the title assumes — the queue-depth pair is two panels because usher.jobs.queued is labelled kind and a priority band exists only in the jobs table, and the enrichment panel splits on outcome because the demand/background split does not exist on that histogram at all.

panels.title: Queue depth by priority band
panels.description: Postgres over jobs.priority, and it is a separate panel from the by-kind gauge beside it rather than the same panel with another datasource. PRD 10 says twice that usher.jobs.queued is labelled kind and not priority — 'JobQueue.depth() counts pending rows per kind, which is what "which lane is backed up" asks' — so a priority band only exists in the table. The four rungs are written out as a spine and LEFT/FULL joined, because a GROUP BY alone returns nothing for an empty queue and an empty rectangle is indistinguishable from a healthy zero. jobs.priority is a free integer (0..100) that promotion moves with GREATEST, so any value off the four rungs still appears, labelled 'off-rung'.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT coalesce(band.name, 'off-rung ' || pending.priority::text) AS priority_band,
       coalesce(band.priority, pending.priority) AS priority,
       coalesce(pending.pending, 0) AS pending
FROM (VALUES ('DEMAND', 100), ('VISIBLE', 80), ('NEW', 50), ('BACKFILL', 20))
         AS band(name, priority)
FULL OUTER JOIN (
    SELECT jobs.priority AS priority, count(*) AS pending
    FROM jobs
    WHERE jobs.status = 'pending'
    GROUP BY jobs.priority
) AS pending ON pending.priority = band.priority
ORDER BY coalesce(band.priority, pending.priority) DESC

panels.title: Queue depth by kind
panels.description: usher.jobs.queued, which reaches Prometheus as usher_jobs_queued_ratio — the exporter puts the instrument's unit (1) in the name. Its only attribute is kind (telemetry.py's _observations emits Observation(count, {"kind": kind})), so this is 'which lane is backed up' and the panel to its left is 'which band is waiting'. Two questions, two panels. The reader is a held snapshot the worker refreshes after each pass, so the value is stale and never wrong; a process with no worker lane reports no observation rather than a zero.

panels.title: Parked jobs by kind
panels.description:
usher.jobs.parked, as usher_jobs_parked_ratio, labelled kind.

⚠️ This series saturates. composition.py's QueueGauges.refresh builds the parked counts from `await queue.parked(limit=1000)` and tallies the returned rows in Python, so the gauge can never sum past 1,000 across all kinds — it is a floor on the parked population and not a count of it. Measured 2026-09-07: the gauge read enrich 890 + index 110 = exactly 1,000 while `SELECT kind, count(*) FROM jobs WHERE status = 'parked' GROUP BY kind` returned enrich 1,890 + index 110 = 2,000. Read this panel as 'at least', and read the table for the number.

panels.title: Enrichment throughput and mean latency
panels.description:
usher.enrichment.latency, as usher_enrichment_latency_seconds. **Its label is outcome, and that is a correction M4 made rather than PRD 10's original.** enrich.py: 'Labelled `outcome` rather than PRD 10's original `trigger`: nothing in M4 enriches on demand (JobPriority.DEMAND is defined and unused until M5), so a `trigger` label would carry one constant value, while a failure's latency and a success's are genuinely different populations.'

⚠️ So the demand-versus-background split a reader of this title expects does not exist on this series. M5 shipped demand promotion and the label did not move: the two values here are `enriched` and `failed`, never `demand` and `background`. Splitting this panel that way needs a second label on the histogram, not a different query.

The rate window is the literal [5m] and not $__rate_interval, which is a portability decision measured on this stack: $__rate_interval is derived from the datasource's configured scrape interval, and a Prometheus fed by remote write from an OTel collector has none — Grafana fell back to 1m15s against a 60 s push interval, which is one sample, and rate() over one sample is empty. Observed 2026-09-07: every rate target on this dashboard returned zero frames until the window was written out.

panels.title: Promotion latency against the 5 s read-through target
panels.description:
Every job promoted to VISIBLE or DEMAND, with the seconds between the promoting enqueue and its last transition, and the traceparent the requesting span put on the row — which is what makes this a join to the trace rather than an estimate.

⚠️ Its population is promotions that did not complete. A completed job's row is DELETED (JobStatus has no DONE member), so a promotion that met the target leaves nothing here. Read this as the miss list, never as a distribution over all promotions.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT jobs.kind AS kind,
       jobs.priority AS priority,
       jobs.status AS status,
       round(extract(epoch FROM (jobs.updated_at - jobs.created_at))::numeric, 3)
           AS seconds_since_promotion,
       jobs.key AS title_id,
       jobs.traceparent AS traceparent
FROM jobs
WHERE jobs.priority >= 80
ORDER BY jobs.updated_at DESC
LIMIT 50

panels.title: Sync run outcomes and duration
panels.description:
sync_runs, which is where the outcome breakdown lives: usher.sync.run.duration carries a status label too, but the histogram only holds runs the *current* process recorded, and this deployment's failures predate it.

No $__timeFilter, deliberately. sync_runs holds this deployment's entire recorded history in ~123 rows, and a window would hide exactly the failed and never-finished runs the panel exists to show. A run still 'running' has no finished_at, so its duration columns are NULL rather than zero.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sync_runs.kind AS kind,
       sync_runs.status AS status,
       count(*) AS runs,
       sum(sync_runs.items_seen) AS items_seen,
       sum(sync_runs.items_unmatched) AS items_unmatched,
       round(avg(extract(epoch FROM
           (sync_runs.finished_at - sync_runs.started_at)))::numeric, 1)
           AS avg_seconds,
       round(max(extract(epoch FROM
           (sync_runs.finished_at - sync_runs.started_at)))::numeric, 1)
           AS max_seconds
FROM sync_runs
GROUP BY sync_runs.kind, sync_runs.status
ORDER BY sync_runs.kind, sync_runs.status

panels.title: Emby request latency by op
panels.description:
usher.source.request.duration, as usher_source_request_duration_seconds, labelled source and op. Two targets on purpose: p95 over the selected window is the live question, and the lifetime mean per op is the reference that keeps the panel readable when the window holds no requests at all — this deployment talks to Emby only while a sync, a watch-state pass or a push lane is running, so an idle window is the ordinary case rather than an outage.

The rate window is the literal [5m] and not $__rate_interval, which is a portability decision measured on this stack: $__rate_interval is derived from the datasource's configured scrape interval, and a Prometheus fed by remote write from an OTel collector has none — Grafana fell back to 1m15s against a 60 s push interval, which is one sample, and rate() over one sample is empty. Observed 2026-09-07: every rate target on this dashboard returned zero frames until the window was written out.

panels.title: Push connection uptime
panels.description:
usher.source.push.connected, as usher_source_push_connected_ratio. **1 means delivering, not connected.** PushSnapshot is fed from PushHealth.is_delivering — connection, at least one message, and a recent one — because a gauge fed by the socket's state would read 1 for a handshake that upgraded against a nonexistent path and was held open.

**The `source` label is the operator-typed source name** ('Shared Emby'), not a UUID: api/lanes.py's push_snapshots builds the reader as {self._names[source_id]: PushSnapshot(...)} over self._open_adapters.

⚠️ **A source with no open lane produces no series at all** — not a zero. It is simply absent from that comprehension, and telemetry.py's _push_observations returns [] with no reader. A disabled source, or one that does not support push, is therefore invisible here rather than reported down. So the Push-down alert condition is `usher_source_push_connected_ratio == 0` for 15m; `absent(...)` would page about every source nobody configured.

The left axis is soft-capped at 1 because the series is 0 or 1: without it Grafana auto-scales a flat zero to 0-100 and a reader has to check the legend to learn the range. Reconnects are cumulative and sit on the right axis.

panels.title: Push events applied, by kind
panels.description:
usher.source.push.events, as usher_source_push_events_total, labelled source and kind. This is what separates 'the lane is up' from 'the lane is doing anything': the cumulative counter is plotted rather than its rate, so a flat line is legible as an idle lane and a missing line as a lane that never delivered that kind.

**The `source` label is the same operator-typed source name the uptime panel carries, and a source with no open lane produces no series here either** — the counter is registered by the same lane. The Push-down alert reads the uptime gauge with `== 0` rather than `absent(...)` for that reason.

panels.title: TMDb requests/sec against the ceiling, with 429 count
panels.description:
usher.provider.requests, as usher_provider_requests_total, labelled provider and status. **status is the HTTP status code as a string** (adapters/tmdb/client.py: `status = str(response.status_code)`) **or the literal "error"** for a transport failure that never reached a status line. Both are recorded from a `finally`, so the rate target selects on provider only and its denominator includes status="error": PRD 10 — 'a denominator that omitted the failures would read low exactly during an outage.'

The ceiling is a named series — `vector(30)` — and not a threshold line. Measured 2026-09-07: as a threshold Grafana drew it against the *right* axis's scale, so a red line labelled nothing appeared at 0.14 req/s on a left axis that had auto-scaled to 0.46. A series carries its own legend entry and pulls the axis to the ceiling, which is what makes headroom the readable quantity. 30 rps is what USHER_TMDB_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND holds — Settings' default is 30.0 and .env.example sets 30. PRD 10's prose said ~40; that figure is not this setting's value at any spelling and the threshold follows the setting.

`or vector(0)` on the 429 target is what makes 'no 429s' render as a zero instead of an empty panel — at the cost that a metric that stopped existing would read the same, which the requests/sec series beside it is what distinguishes.

The rate window is the literal [5m] and not $__rate_interval, which is a portability decision measured on this stack: $__rate_interval is derived from the datasource's configured scrape interval, and a Prometheus fed by remote write from an OTel collector has none — Grafana fell back to 1m15s against a 60 s push interval, which is one sample, and rate() over one sample is empty. Observed 2026-09-07: every rate target on this dashboard returned zero frames until the window was written out.
